text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I sketched a small phased refactor for the intake/triage path. goal: make compatibility checks cheaper and isolate heavy benches from fast smoke. thoughts?
kevin: +1 to phases. can you outline the phases?
san: Agree. We keep seeing tail latency spikes when full bench runs kick in during ingest. separating is 👍
maria: Plan idea: Phase 1: lightweight triage (fast fingerprints + minimal tensor checks). Phase 2: shim adapters that normalize model metadata for bench harness. Phase 3: backfill full bench asynchronously with soft-fail for infra-limited models.
julia: For Phase 1, what are acceptable heuristics? size/param count + simple forward pass correctness?
arun: Suggest: fingerprints (sha1 of model binary + config), param count, tokenizer sanity (sample tokenization on 20 prompts), and a 100-sample latency smoke at max sequence length. keep it <30s total.
kevin: Love that. Also add a lightweight kv-cache exercise to ensure caching hooks don't blow memory for big seq len. a single-step allocation probe should catch most issues.
maria: Good call. For Phase 2 (shim), the idea is a small adapter layer that maps model inputs/outputs to bench harness expected shapes + explicit quantization metadata. The shim runs in a container with constrained resources so it mirrors runtime.
san: How will we validate shim correctness? we need deterministic golden outputs for a few canonical prompts per model family. store golden artifacts in GCS and compare on float-tolerant diffs.
julia: Tolerant diffs: use relative L2 on logits + cosine on embeddings. we should surface threshold breaches in the console as "quality regression" not hard block.
maria: Phase 3 backfill: full bench (throughput/latency/quality suites) runs on dedicated bench fleet. If full bench fails due to infra, we mark model as "pending full bench" but still allow canary small traffic with strict SLOs.
kevin: Ops question: who is oncall for bench infra during rollout? bench-bot: bench-bot: scheduled run created: `bench-run/5267890123-intake-triage` assigned to @kevin, @arun. ETA 2h.
arun: I'll take first run. what metrics should we assert automatically?
maria: Auto-asserts: p99 latency < 300ms for small models (<10B) on dedicated hw profile, mean tokens/sec > baseline, error rate <0.1%, tokenizer fail count = 0, mem alloc within headroom. Also regression delta vs golden model for quality: embedding cosine drop < 0.02.
san: Also capture failure types: OOM, unsupported op, tokenizer crash, unexpected model outputs. map those back to actionable tickets (shim update, converter fix, runtime kernel selection).
julia: For rollout, propose gating: triage pass -> shim created -> canary (1% traffic) with health checks -> full bench backfill. If canary regresses quality or latency exceed threshold, auto-rollback to fallback model variant.
kevin: Can we reuse existing rollout infra? or need a new lightweight pipeline?
maria: Reuse rollout infra but add a new "triage" step in the pipeline UI and a flag to mark model as "triaged". UI should show triage log, shim diff, golden-compare histogram.
arun: I'll start a quick PR to add triage step metadata to model registry and a REST endpoint `/v1/models/:id/triage` that returns triage status + logs.
san: For benchmarks, I'll prepare a 100-sample canonical set per model family and a generator that expands with seeds. also need a compact canonical tokenizer test set to catch tokenization edgecases.
kevin: CI: let's gate the triage run in PRs for model adapters and converters. and add a nightly full-backfill pipeline for models marked pending.
maria: Action items: 1) @arun create registry endpoint + PR for triage metadata. 2) @san prepare canonical prompt sets + tokenizer suite. 3) @kevin run initial triage/bench with bench-bot and report failures. 4) @julia wire console UI elements for triage view. I'll draft a short RFC for this flow tonight.
julia: acked, will prototype UI mockups.
kevin: Running bench now. command I used: `./bench/run_smoke.sh --samples=100 --max-seq=1024 --timeout=2m --model-id=tmp-5267` will post logs here.
arun: If bench-bot posts artifacts, link them in thread so we can triage quickly.
maria: Thanks all. keeping this lightweight will let us onboard experimental models faster without noisy full benches. we'll iterate on thresholds after first 10 models. :wave:
